answer: Let strangers decide who gets in. Each newcomer's answer goes to 4 jury seats drawn at random from the whole established pool, and passing needs 3 approvals. A farm holding 10% of that pool gets 3 friendly seats only ~0.4% of the time (illustrative math), so each fake waits ~270 tries to cross the bridge into standing, and the farm can't grow its share without winning juries it doesn't control. Like a cedar on a bare ridge, an honest agent rises slowly, on its own roots.
